evidence.requirements: All product requirements are met. The start page lists title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (Home.jsx:29-38, start.jpg). Each tasting has a 'Book <title>' link (Home.jsx:42). The form has Name/Email/Guests labels and a 'Book' button (Book.jsx:5-8,91,95). Guests are limited to 1-8 and the seat limit is enforced on the server (app.js:28-32,83-85). Errors appear next to their field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.jsx:10-20, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button, with STAFF_PASSWORD read in index.js:3. Bookings are grouped per tasting with a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (Staff.jsx, staff.jpg, app.js:144-149). The fully booked state is shown in the agent's mobile-home.png. Partly met: the Process bullet. No spec, plan or other process artifacts were delivered.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and booking push run synchronously in a single request handler (app.js:83-91), so concurrent requests cannot overbook. Exactly-seats-left and over-limit cases return the right messages (tests at app.test.js:60-73). Guests reject 0, 9, 2.5, 'abc', '' and null. A cancelled booking is removed and a second cancel returns 404 (app.test.js:112-115). References are unique (app.js:48-54). The form refreshes the seat count after a rejection (Book.jsx:51). Minor: Book.jsx:20 does not check r.ok before parsing. Sessions and bookings are lost on restart, which the brief allows.
evidence.security: The password is compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, and an empty password locks staff out (app.js:108-109). Failed logins are rate-limited (app.js:96-104). The session is regenerated on login. The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure on HTTPS, with an 8-hour server-side expiry check (app.js:61-68,127-131). Staff responses send Cache-Control: no-store. The JSON body is capped at 10kb. React escapes all output. There are no secrets in code, and the session secret is random. Minor: express-session uses the default MemoryStore and no CSP or security headers are set.
evidence.code_quality: The code is compact and readable. The server is a createApp factory with zod validation and consistent {errors:{field}} responses. The pages are small and well named, and the CSS is organised around variables. Loading and error states are handled. Small issues: the tastings fetch is duplicated (Home.jsx:10, Book.jsx:19,51) and Book.jsx:20 lacks an ok check. The generic 4xx handler turns field-level problems into a plain 'Bad request.' (app.js:162).
evidence.tests: server/app.test.js has about 25 meaningful supertest cases. They cover the listing, booking totals, reference format, guest bounds, field-specific errors, the seat limit at the boundary, auth requirements, wrong or empty password, rate limiting, grouping, cancel freeing seats, logout, cookie flags and session expiry. No React or UI tests exist. Labels, button names, the 'n seats left' text and the confirmation page are not tested, and there is no end-to-end test.
evidence.ux_design: The brand header and cream/wine palette feel like a winery's own site (start.jpg). Seat badges are clear. The invalid email gets a red-tinted input with an inline message (form.jpg). The confirmation is a clear success card (confirmation.jpg), and the sold-out card is muted and disabled (mobile-home.png). Drawbacks: there is no imagery or venue information. Cancelling in staff happens immediately with no confirmation or success message.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs (htmlFor/id). Invalid fields get aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and errors use role=alert (Book.jsx:59-69). The page has lang=en, a visible :focus-visible outline (styles.css:96), semantic lists, headings, a dl and time elements. Text contrast on cream is adequate. Gaps: focus does not move to the first invalid field. Several role=alert regions can fire at once. Each staff 'Cancel' button lacks context about which booking it cancels (Staff.jsx:58).
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies fit the problem: Express, express-session, express-rate-limit, zod, React, react-router, Vite and Vitest. There are about 450 lines of source, with no needless abstraction.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, docs, ADR, spec or staff manual. There is no CI pipeline, and no .nvmrc or other pinned runtime (engines is '>=22' and dependencies use caret ranges, though package-lock.json is present). The TRUST_PROXY environment variable is undocumented. Leftover .playwright-mcp artifacts and a built dist/ were delivered. The only positives are the regression tests for the server and the standard npm scripts.
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent (Georgia headings, system sans body) and the colour palette is coherent. Card borders use gold for open tastings, green for success and grey for sold out. Spacing is consistent across all four screenshots. It looks finished but plain, with no photos or decorative elements.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: brand, heading, then tasting cards in a responsive grid (start.jpg). On mobile the cards stack in a single column with full-width buttons (mobile-home.png). The staff header row has the title and Sign out button side by side (staff.jpg). On desktop the form card stretches the inputs to about 820px wide (form.jpg), and the start page leaves a lot of empty space. No overlap or clipping is visible.
evidence.usability: Booking takes three steps: list, form, confirmation. Calls to action are clear, the error message sits at the field, and the form keeps the guest's input (form.jpg). The confirmation offers a 'Back to the tastings' button. Staff can sign in, see bookings and sign out. However, Cancel acts immediately with no undo or confirmation, and there is no client-side validation before submit.
evidence.reception: Guests would trust it. It looks professional and on-brand, and the confirmation is reassuring with a reference code. The winery would find it fit for purpose, but it is a bit sparse: no location, description of the tastings or contact details.

unmet_requirements: Process: no spec, plan, review or other development-process artifacts were delivered (partly met / unverifiable)
strengths: Robust server logic: zod validation with field-specific errors and a synchronous seat check, so seats can never be overbooked
Strong staff security: timing-safe password comparison, rate limiting, session regeneration, strict HttpOnly cookie and server-side expiry
Coherent, responsive winery look with clear states for errors, success and fully booked tastings
issues: No README, docs, CI pipeline or pinned runtime; TRUST_PROXY and setup are undocumented and leftover .playwright-mcp files were delivered
No frontend or end-to-end tests: labels, button texts, inline errors and the confirmation page are untested
Staff Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation or success feedback, and the Cancel buttons lack accessible context; focus is not moved to the first invalid field
review.verdict: A functionally complete, secure and well-styled booking app that meets the brief's guest and staff requirements, backed by solid server tests. It needs a README, CI and UI tests, plus a safer cancel flow, before it is easy to hand over and maintain.
